The pay revision will cost ₹ 52 crore, with increased wages transferred directly to workers’ bank accounts. Jocelyn Fernandes Updated 26 Oct 2026, 10:25 AM IST Prefer Livemint on Google 4,000 Delhi Municipal Corporation public health workers will receive higher wages of ₹18,000 and dearness allowance under a pay revision. ( AFP Photo / Indranil Mukherjee ) AI Quick Read DA news, wage hike: As many as 4,000 public health workers employed with the Delhi Municipal Corporation ( MCD ) are set to see an increase in their wages and receive dearness allowance, officials in the national capital announced. The pay revision, which was made public at an event on Friday by Delhi CM Rekha Gupta , will cost the exchequer ₹ 52 crore, PTI reported. Wage hike, DA for MCD workers: What we know About 4,000 of the MCD's public health workers will receive a minimum monthly salary of ₹ 18,000, along with dearness allowance, under the principle of equal pay for equal work, according to the report. Also Read | Elon Musk says SpaceX closed $40 billion debt deal for AI chips — What we know The employees who were designated as domestic breeding checker (DBC) staff and later redesignated as Multi-Tasking Staff ( Public Health ) were recruited to help contain dengue. They have continued to perform public health duties, including door-to-door visits, over the years, MCD Commissioner Sanjeev Khirwar said in a statement. Under the revised arrangement, their salaries will be fixed at the minimum of Level 1 of the pay matrix, or ₹ 18,000, in addition to variable dearness allowance. The increased wages have been transferred directly to their bank accounts, Mayor Pravesh Wahi said. Also Read | Bank holiday today: Are SBI, HDFC, ICICI closed on 26 October for Laxmi Puja? Recognise employees who worked for decades in public health According to Wahi, the proposal for the wage increase and DA had been announced in the previous budget and was brought before the chief minister for approval. CM Gupta said the implementation recognises the contribution of employees who had worked for decades in public health. She added that the government had a responsibility to address their welfare. “It is our duty to care for the thousands of employees who serve Delhi,” she said, according to a statement issued by the mayor's office. Recruitment of 2,500 sanitation workers The pay revision comes amid the MCD's efforts to address employee-related issues, with the mayor also announcing the recruitment of 2,500 sanitation workers ahead of Diwali to improve cleanliness in the city and its markets, the report added. Earlier, Gupta directed the MCD to launch night-time cleaning drives in major markets and residential colonies, amid complaints about garbage accumulation and delays in waste collection across parts of the capital. The order aims to improve cleanliness across Delhi, when markets and public spaces typically see increased footfall during the festive rush. The chief minister has warned that negligence in sanitation will not be tolerated and instructed civic officials to ensure that improvements are visible on the ground.
